data.title: RB Global Shares Rise on Expanded Buyback Program to $1B
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

RB Global shares advanced Tuesday after the company said that it has doubled the dollar amount of its share-repurchase ceiling to $1 billion.

Shares were up 2.1% in Toronto at 119.32 Canadian dollars. Its New York shares were rising 2.3%.

The commercial assets and vehicles marketplace on Tuesday said the Toronto Stock Exchange has approved an amendment to its current share-repurchase program allowing it to buy back up to about 14.2 million shares, or about 10% of its public float, up to $1 billion.

Previously the company had a target to buy back up to 10 million shares, or about 7% of the total public float up to a maximum of $500 million.

Its Toronto shares have been under pressure in 2026, falling about 16% since the year began.

As of Sept. 11, the company has repurchased about 5.36 million shares at an average price of $93.22, it said.

Write to Adriano Marchese at adriano.marchese@wsj.com

data.title: How Long Will Benchmark Treasury Yield Stay Above 5%? — WSJ
data.description:
By WSJ Staff

The 10-year Treasury yield has popped up above 5% for the second straight day. Many investors are probably wondering how long it might stay there.

If recent history is any guide, the answer is: not that long. The past eight times the Treasury yield closed above 5%, it went back down below that level in less than two months, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The average number of trading days it stayed above 5% was 12. All those stretches occurred in 2006 and 2007.

Longer periods of 10-year yields staying above 5% happened in 2002, 2001 and 1999-2000. Before September 1998, the 10-year yield was above 5% for more than two decades.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Zoom Moves Into Sales Software With Engage and Forecast
data.description:
Zoom Communications Inc. fell 0.95% intraday as it unveiled what it calls an AI-powered revenue operating system, adding two capabilities

to Zoom Revenue Accelerator and making Common Room available through its own channel.

These additions point at different parts of the sales process. Engage builds multichannel outreach sequences across email and phone, prioritizes follow-up and uses automated triggers to reach prospects at scale. Forecast turns deal-level signals into a live forecast, letting leaders drill from company commitments down to individual opportunities, with revenue operations teams able to configure views and write updates back to the CRM without engineering support.

Zoom argues the calls happening on its platform contain what a buyer cares about, the objections raised, who is involved in a decision and what was agreed, and that connecting that to prospecting and forecasting creates a continuous loop. Barracuda Networks, a Zoom customer, reported a 15% increase in deals closed and 5% faster deal velocity using Revenue Accelerator. The product now sells in three tiers, with the new Elite level including both Engage and Forecast.

data.title: Vodafone Idea Fined Rs 2 Lakh By Trai For QoS Breach
data.description:
The order comes as Trai reviews its Quality of Service framework, and telecom operators face continued scrutiny over network performance

Vodafone Idea (Vi) has been imposed a financial disincentive of Rs 2 lakh by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) for failing to comply with prescribed Quality of Service (QoS) standards in various areas during October 2025. The telecom operator received the order on 14 September 2026 and disclosed the development in a stock exchange filing on 15 September.

The order relates to non-compliance with the Standards of Quality of Service of Access (Wireline and Wireless) and Broadband (Wireline and Wireless) Service Regulations, 2024. Vi said the maximum financial impact from the order is limited to the disincentive levied by TRAI.

Vi said it is reviewing the order and evaluating the next steps in the matter. The company did not disclose any additional operational or financial impact arising from the regulatory action.

The filing was made pursuant to Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) Listing Regulations. The company has not provided details of the specific QoS parameters or service areas that resulted in the latest disincentive.

Trai’s QoS framework requires telecom service providers to meet prescribed service benchmarks. Where operators fail to meet the stipulated benchmarks, the regulator seeks an explanation from the service provider before deciding on any financial disincentive.

Wider QoS Scrutiny

The latest order comes amid broader regulatory scrutiny of service quality across India’s telecom sector. Parliament was informed in August that telecom operators had faced a combined Rs 1.9 crore in penalties for QoS violations during FY26, with BSNL accounting for the highest amount at Rs 57.5 lakh, followed by Bharti Airtel at Rs 48 lakh, MTNL at Rs 37 lakh, Vodafone Idea at Rs 31 lakh and Reliance Jio at Rs 17 lakh.

The Rs 2 lakh disincentive disclosed by Vi on September 15 is a separate regulatory order and should not be treated as part of the Rs 31 lakh figure reported for FY26. The earlier figure represents penalties imposed on the company during the financial year, while the latest disclosure relates specifically to the October 2025 QoS non-compliance matter.

Trai Reviews QoS Rules

Trai is also examining changes to its QoS framework. In August 2026, the regulator issued a consultation paper on proposed amendments to the 2024 Standards of Quality of Service of Access and Broadband Services Regulations, with Vodafone Idea among the telecom operators that submitted comments.

The proposed review covers the existing QoS framework for wireless and wireline access and broadband services. The development comes as operators face closer scrutiny over network performance and compliance with prescribed service standards.

For Vi, the latest Rs 2 lakh order has limited financial significance based on the company’s filing. However, the disclosure comes against a wider regulatory focus on telecom service quality and the enforcement of QoS requirements across operators.

data.title: Mazagon Dock Signs MoU For Rs 27,000 Cr Greenfield Shipbuilding Cluster
data.description:
The Dighi facility will target 2 million gross tonnes of annual shipbuilding capacity, supporting large commercial vessel construction in Maharashtra

Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders (MDL) will invest around Rs 27,000 crore to establish a greenfield shipbuilding cluster at Dighi in Maharashtra’s Raigad district. The project is expected to generate around 90,000 jobs, the Maharashtra government said on Tuesday.

MDL signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Maharashtra Ltd (NSHIPML) in the presence of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. The agreement is aimed at developing the proposed shipbuilding facility at Dighi, according to an official release.

As per the agreement, MDL has set a target of achieving an annual shipbuilding capacity of at least 2 million gross tonnes at Dighi. The project will enable the construction of large commercial vessels and strengthen the country’s maritime industrial capabilities, the release said.

The proposed Rs 27,000 crore investment will support the development of modern shipbuilding infrastructure at the site. It will also create an industrial and supply chain ecosystem aimed at supporting activities across the shipbuilding sector.

Cluster Development Plan

The greenfield shipbuilding cluster is being developed jointly by the Maharashtra Maritime Board and the Mumbai Port Authority through NSHIPML. The special-purpose company was established specifically to take forward the development of the proposed cluster.

The project is being taken forward under the Centre’s Greenfield Shipbuilding Cluster Development Plan and is expected to complement the objectives of the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. The initiative is expected to strengthen India’s maritime industrial capabilities.

According to the release, the Dighi project is expected to boost domestic shipbuilding capacity, attract technology and investment, and create skilled employment opportunities. It is also expected to enhance India’s competitiveness in the global maritime sector.

The proposed cluster will provide modern shipbuilding infrastructure alongside an industrial and supply chain ecosystem. The development is expected to support the wider maritime sector through increased capacity and related industrial activity.

MDL Chairman and Managing Director Captain Jagmohan said the company would work towards creating a modern, globally competitive shipbuilding facility at Dighi with the cooperation of all stakeholders. He said the facility would be developed with support from stakeholders involved in the project.

Captain Jagmohan signed the MoU with NSHIPML Managing Director Pradeep P, the release said. The agreement marks MDL’s proposed participation in the development of the Dighi greenfield shipbuilding cluster.

data.title: Euro zone yields hit multi-year highs, EU borrowing costs jump
data.description:
Key points:
  • German 10-year yield hits 17-year high
  • EU sells debt at highest yield since 2020
  • Rising Fed rate hike bets add to pressure
  • Inflation and government debt worries weigh

By Harry Robertson

Benchmark euro zone borrowing costs rose to their highest in 17 years on Tuesday, with a weeks-long selloff gathering new momentum as conflict in the Middle East pushed up oil prices and U.S. yields surged.

The impact of rising yields was seen in a sale of debt by the European Union, which faced its highest borrowing costs since it became a major issuer in 2020 on Tuesday.

Germany's 10-year bond yield (DE10YT=RR) rose more than 4 basis points to 3.572%, its highest since 2011, before slipping back to stand 1 bp higher. Yields rise as prices fall.

Longer-dated bonds, which reflect expectations about inflation, the economy and public debt, fell most sharply. France's 30-year yield (FR30YT=RR) hit its highest since 2002 near 5.2% and Germany's equivalent yield (DE30YT=RR) touched a 15-year peak above 3.9%.

Bond yields, which determine the cost of new borrowing, have hit multi-year or even multi-decade highs around the world in recent weeks.

Rising energy prices have caused traders to ramp up bets on rate hikes, while worries about government debt levels and corporate bond issuance to fund AI have added to the pressure on bond markets.

U.S. Treasury yields rose sharply on Tuesday as investors braced for a Federal Reserve rate hike, with the benchmark 10-year borrowing cost hitting its highest since 2007 at 5.041%.

"The U.S. is leading the way and we believe that short-term expectations of the Fed are the main driver for the longer maturities as well," said Marcus Widen, an economist at SEB.

"The rise in interest rates is directly linked to the deteriorating situation in energy prices."

Advances by Yemen's Houthis and drone attacks that closed Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, a key export route that bypassed the now-treacherous Strait of Hormuz, pushed up oil prices this week.

Brent crude was last trading 1.5% higher at $107 a barrel after the Houthis launched new attacks and Gulf Arab states postponed planned talks with Iran over the war.

EU BORROWS AT HIGHEST YIELD SINCE 2020

The EU sold €5 billion ($5.8 billion) of new 30-year bonds via a syndicate of banks on Tuesday at a yield of 4.541%, according to a lead manager memo seen by Reuters.

That would be the highest yield paid on any bond since the EU began large-scale borrowing to support economies during the COVID-19 pandemic more than six years ago, according to European Commission data. It is up sharply from a yield of 4.214% paid during a tap of a 30-year bond in May.

The key event for markets this week is the Fed decision on Wednesday. Traders now expect a rate hike after inflation remained elevated in August and as the Iran conflict shows few signs of ending.

Shorter-dated euro zone bonds, which reflect bets on the European Central Bank rate outlook, slipped back on Tuesday but remained close to the previous day's highs.

Germany's 2-year bond yield (DE2YT=RR) was down 2 bps at 3.25%, after rising above 3.31% on Monday, the highest in three years.

The ECB raised interest rates last week to try to stop inflation spreading through the economy, and money markets are pricing in another hike this year as well as two or more next year.

France's government debt came under renewed pressure, reflecting investor nerves about next year's election and upcoming battles over the country's budget deficit.

The gap between French and German 10-year yields (DE10FR10=RR), a reflection of the risk premium attached to French debt, rose to its highest since 2012 at more than 98 bps.
